analysis.title: USA: Housing Starts Above Consensus Expectations; Building Permits Well Below Consensus Expectations
key_insights: October housing starts rose 9.9% to 1,309k SAAR, above the GS forecast of +4.6% (1,277k) and the median forecast of +2.4% (1,250k).
The starts increase came mainly from multi-family starts (+23.6% month-over-month), which are more volatile than single-family starts (+4.0%).
September starts growth was revised down 1.8pp to -7.0% (1,191k SAAR). Starts have swung by an average of 11.1% month-over-month over the past six months.
October building permits fell 7.4% to 1,295k SAAR, well below the median forecast of -1.7% (1,375k). Single-family permits fell 8.7% and multi-family permits fell 5.3%.

GS reads the permit weakness as consistent with its view that housing activity will contract further in the coming quarters, with higher interest rates weighing on single-family starts over the next year.
GS left its Q4 GDP tracking estimate unchanged at +2.4% (quarter-over-quarter annualized) and its past-quarter tracking estimate unchanged at +3.8%.

sector_views.rationale: Permits fell well below consensus, which GS says points to further contraction in housing activity, with higher interest rates weighing on single-family starts over the next year.
